sources.title: Insa Nolte, Yoruba Histories of Marriage and Belonging
sources.note: First online 16 June 2025, Gender and History 38(2), pages 497 to 514. Full article checked: urban quarters, family traditions and Ondo Eku festival dated by cited Olupona to Terere 1770 to 1795. Treat oral narratives critically, not as contemporaneous eyewitness transcripts.

sources.title: Titilayo Tilewola Nwaokoro, Women Education and Social Change in Ondo, 1875 to 2008 (2013)
sources.note: Full245-page University of Ibadan thesis now directly accessible via new repository download. Markets/slave trade printed pp32 to 33/PDF45 to 46; household training pp39 to 40/PDF52 to 53; education figures abstract p.v. The broad claim that European rule eradicated slavery is not adopted.

sources.title: Abidemi Babatunde Babalola, Ancient History of Technology in West Africa (2017)
sources.note: Journal of Black Studies 48(5), pages 501 to 527. Investigator’s account of 2011 to 2012 Igbo Olokun trenches, dates, almost13000 beads and over800 crucible fragments.

sources.title: Babalola and colleagues, Chemical analysis of glass beads from Igbo Olokun (2018)
sources.note: Journal of Archaeological Science90, pages92 to 105, DOI10.1016/j.jas.2017.12.005. High-lime/high-alumina composition and local raw materials support primary glass production, not merely imported beads.

sources.title: Léa Roth, Excavations at Lujumo Compound, Ife: preliminary report
sources.note: Primary 2022 excavation account. Three pavement levels; medieval12th to 13th-century deposits under a probably late19th-century family house. Pavement roles include erosion management; no proven citywide sewer or toilet system inferred.

sources.title: Amanda L. Logan and colleagues, Early archaeological evidence of wheat and cotton from medieval Ile-Ife (2024)
sources.note: PNAS121(37), e2403256121. Full indexed original checked. Wheat48 secure grains plus7 tentative; two direct dates broadly late13th to 14th centuries. Cotton late12th to early13th. Import/local cultivation distinctions retained.

sources.title: UNESCO, Ifa divination system
sources.note: Living-heritage dossier proclaimed2005 and inscribed2008. English endpoint returned minimal text; full official Spanish and French equivalents directly checked.256 odu and poetic ese are oral knowledge/sign systems, not a dated eighteenth-century manuscript.

sources.title: S. A. Akintoye, The Ondo road Eastwards of Lagos, c.1870 to 95 (1969)
sources.note: African Union library provides scholarly abstract, Journal of African History10(4), pp581 to 598. Route, agricultural/manufacturing growth and missionary schools after1870, explicitly later than atlas.

proposedOverrides.name: Southwestern Nigerian communities (atlas label “Africa”)
proposedOverrides.summary: Local histories around Ife and Ondo, beneath a misleading continental atlas label.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed ID only. Imported1783 to 1815 polygon is not continental, despite its name. Public display name and overview correct this mismatch. No claim of exact identity with one Yoruba kingdom; no aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Both slices identical; bbox3.9510395,6.0027282 to5.0562506,7.7802275. Ife and Ondo approximate points inside; Ilesa, Ijebu-Ode, Ijebu-Igbo, Owo, Old Oyo, Lagos, Abeokuta and Benin City outside. The1800 seam is not a political event.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Two directly map-relevant historical discussions concern Terere1770 to 1795 and eighteenth-century trade. Wider retrospective settlement/market history is marked. Medieval glass, wheat, cotton and pavements are explicitly centuries earlier. Late nineteenth-century house,1870road,1875school and modern Ifa/language evidence are explicitly later. Evidence does not justify a homogeneous1783state.
batchIdentityNotes.limitations: No specific exact-window household toilet, hospital or medicine preparation verified. Erosion-management surfaces are not sewers. Oral traditions are historical sources requiring criticism. Modern Yoruba vocabulary is dated to its actual scholarly witness; no ancient script fabricated. Thesis sweeping generalizations about all Africa and claims of colonial eradication of slavery were not adopted.
